title: Secure Access to Virtual Networks

header.html: Create and configure network security groups (NSGs) and application security groups; evaluate effective security rules in NSGs; implement Azure Bastion; configure service endpoints for Azure platform as a service (PaaS); configure private endpoints for Azure PaaS
the official Microsoft Learn AZ-104 study guide, skills measured as of October 26, 2023

html:
1Network security groups (NSGs)

An NSG is a list of allow and deny rules that filters inbound and outbound traffic to Azure resources. Associate it with a subnet or a network interface (NIC).

Rule property Meaning
Priority 100 to 4096; lower number is processed first; processing stops at the first match
Source / destination IP address, CIDR, service tag, or application security group
Protocol and port TCP, UDP, ICMP, or Any; port or range
Action Allow or Deny
Direction Inbound or Outbound

Default rules (cannot be deleted, priority 65000 and above): AllowVnetInBound, AllowAzureLoadBalancerInBound, DenyAllInBound; outbound: AllowVnetOutBound, AllowInternetOutBound, DenyAllOutBound.

Service tags (for example Internet, VirtualNetwork, Storage, AzureLoadBalancer) stand for groups of IP prefixes that Microsoft maintains.

2Application security groups (ASGs)

An ASG lets you group VMs by role (web servers, database servers) and use the group as the source or destination in NSG rules, instead of IP addresses.

Exam tip

. "Allow web servers to reach database servers on port 1433 without listing IP addresses" = NSG rule between application security groups.

3Effective security rules

If both a subnet NSG and a NIC NSG exist, both are evaluated: inbound traffic passes the subnet NSG first, then the NIC NSG; outbound the reverse. Traffic must be allowed by both.

Tool Shows
Effective security rules (NIC blade) The combined result of all NSGs on a NIC
IP flow verify Allowed or denied for a given flow, and which rule

4Azure Bastion

Azure Bastion gives secure RDP and SSH to VMs directly from the Azure portal over TLS (port 443), without public IP addresses on the VMs.

Fact Detail
Subnet A dedicated subnet named AzureBastionSubnet, at least /26
SKUs Developer, Basic, Standard, Premium with growing features [Verify live]
Benefit No inbound RDP or SSH ports exposed to the internet
Exam tip

. "Connect to VMs by RDP or SSH securely with no public IPs and no open ports" = Azure Bastion.

5Service endpoints and private endpoints

Feature Service endpoint Private endpoint
What it is Extends the VNet identity to the service over the Azure backbone A network interface with a private IP in your VNet that maps to one instance of the service
Service IP Still the service's public IP A private IP from your subnet
Reach from on-premises No Yes, through VPN or ExpressRoute
DNS No change Needs a private DNS zone (for example privatelink.blob.core.windows.net)
Cost Free Charged (per endpoint and data)
Use Simple, free subnet restriction Fully private access, data exfiltration protection
Exam tip

. On-premises access over a private connection, or a private IP for the PaaS service = private endpoint. Subnet-only restriction at no cost = service endpoint.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Two NSG rules apply to the same traffic: priority 200 allows it and priority 300 denies it. What is the result?

  • AAllowed, because the lower number is processed first
  • BDenied, because the highest priority number wins
  • CBoth applied, with the deny taking effect only after the allow expires
  • DNeither applied, because conflicting rules cancel each other out
Show the answer

Answer: A. Rules are processed from the lowest priority number and the first match wins.

S2Web servers must be allowed to reach database servers on one port without using IP addresses. What should be used?

  • AApplication security groups in NSG rules
  • BA route table that sends traffic between the two groups of servers
  • CA budget alert that fires when the database servers receive traffic
  • DA tag on each VM that lists the servers allowed to connect to it
Show the answer

Answer: A. ASGs group VMs by role for use in rules.

S3Administrators need RDP and SSH to VMs that have no public IPs and no open inbound ports. What fits?

  • AA VPN to every VM
  • BAzure Bastion
  • CA public IP on each VM
  • DA Delete lock
Show the answer

Answer: B. Bastion provides TLS-based access from the portal.

S4What is the required name for the Azure Bastion subnet?

  • ABastionSubnet
  • BAzureBastionSubnet
  • CGatewaySubnet
  • DDefaultSubnet
Show the answer

Answer: B. The dedicated subnet must be named AzureBastionSubnet.

S5An on-premises network must reach an Azure storage account over a private connection. What fits?

  • AA service endpoint
  • BA public IP
  • CA private endpoint
  • DA tag
Show the answer

Answer: C. Private endpoints are reachable from on-premises through VPN or ExpressRoute.

S6A VM has an NSG on both its subnet and its NIC. What must be true for inbound traffic to reach it?

  • AEither NSG may allow it
  • BBoth NSGs must allow it
  • COnly the subnet NSG matters
  • DOnly the NIC NSG matters
Show the answer

Answer: B. Traffic is evaluated by both NSGs.

6.2 Recall questions

R1What decides which NSG rule applies first?

Show the answer

The lowest priority number.

R2Name one default inbound NSG rule.

Show the answer

For example AllowVnetInBound or DenyAllInBound.

R3What does an application security group do?

Show the answer

Groups VMs by role for use in NSG rules.

R4What port does Bastion use from the browser?

Show the answer

443 over TLS.

R5Which endpoint type gives a private IP in your VNet?

Show the answer

A private endpoint.

R6What DNS setup does a private endpoint need?

Show the answer

A private DNS zone for the service.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact

ASG group VMs by role for rules
Effective rules subnet and NIC NSGs both apply; IP flow verify
Bastion AzureBastionSubnet /26, RDP/SSH over TLS, no public IP
Endpoints service endpoint (free, public IP of service) vs private endpoint (private IP, on-premises reach, private DNS)
